audience.programmeDescription: Communication and Life Sciences studies how communication and media shape societal change around health, food, climate and other life-science issues. Communication theory, social research and a chosen life-science field connect science with public and professional audiences.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete comparison is withheld while the applicable curriculum, approved life-science course package and thesis-entry requirements are verified. The earlier handbook and related UCR research are retained, but do not establish a complete current pathway.

provisionalCourseDescriptions.name: Personal & Professional Development
provisionalCourseDescriptions.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

provisionalCourseDescriptions.name: Governance of Sustainability
provisionalCourseDescriptions.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.

Students compare legal traditions and study public and private law, human rights, justice, social control and change, race and gender. Case briefs, demand letters and mock trials develop legal reasoning, while a family-law topic supports the design of a socio-legal research proposal.
